title: Adaptive dialogue coalescer and KV granularity tuning for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Elena García
description: Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts with long streaming responses, and multi-turn dialogues with long histories) create fragmentation in the continuous batching scheduler and cause KV cache residency churn. On current runtime-1.20 profiles we see CPU-side scheduling overhead and GPU memory fragmentation causing up to a 32% throughput drop during skewed dialogue bursts. Goal: Design and ship an adaptive coalescer scheduler plus KV cache granularity changes to reduce end-to-end p95 latency by 20% on skewed workloads while improving GPU memory utilization and keeping average token cost within 5% of baseline. This ticket covers design, experiments, and the rollout plan for runtime-1.22.
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler reduces p95 token latency for mixed prompt/response traces by >=20% on our benchmark cluster (NVIDIA L4, 8x replicas)
KV cache fragmentation (measured as number of evictions per minute) reduced by >=30% under synthetic skewed-dialogue load
No regression in overall throughput (>95% of baseline) for balanced workloads
Automated canary rollout with metric-based rollback and dashboard panels added to Console runtime-1.22 release page
Design doc and implementation PRs reviewed by infra and applied-ml teams

2026-02-19 - Marco Ruiz: Baseline run (cluster: perf-staging-03). Observed metrics: tail-latency spikes correlated with long-response streams; KV eviction spikes during 30–90s burst windows. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.company/runtime/benchmarks/773456/baseline

2026-02-22 - Liang Chen (applied-ml): Proposed two knobs: 1) coalescer window that dynamically shrinks when long-response tokens are present, 2) KV-object-level granularity (per-turn vs per-token prefix) to delay eviction. Both require kernel-friendly layout changes for the runtime.

2026-02-25 - Design review (attendees: Marco, Liang, Aisha, Riley): Trade-offs identified: larger coalescer windows improve throughput but increase latency for short prompts; fine-grained KV objects reduce unnecessary evicts but increase metadata overhead. Decision: implement adaptive coalescer that uses recent length histogram and per-connection priority score and implement a hybrid KV object model (turn-level primary, per-prefix secondary cache) behind a runtime flag.

2026-02-27 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype implemented in branch feature/eng/773456-adaptive-coalescer. Microbenchmarks: p95 reduced by 18% on synthetic skewed-dialogue; KV evictions down 27% but memory overhead +2.6%.

2026-03-01 - Performance review: Applied-ML requests additional check for generation quality under changed coalescing because batching timing can alter decoder step interleaving. Added small-quality-eval suite to CI.

2026-03-02 - Marco Ruiz: Preparing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/13421. Will include feature flag runtime.coalescer.adaptive_v1 and kv.hybrid_object_v1. Next: run canary with dedicated pool and validate rollback thresholds.
notes: Experiment summary: We ran three workload classes: (A) short-prompt long-response streaming (LLM-chatbot), (B) multi-turn long-history queries (assistant with context), (C) balanced synthetic. Results: A: p95 token latency -22% (good), evictions -34%; B: p95 -16%, evictions -29%; C: throughput -3% (within target). Concerns: metadata overhead for hybrid KV model increased software-managed memory by ~2–3% — will instrument allocator to avoid high-water surprises. Rollout plan: feature-flagged canary (10%), metric-slo guardrails (p50/p95 tokens, evictions/min, GPU-allocated-memory), 24h watch, gradual ramp to 50% then 100% if stable.
